from_notes: P4 = Public-Private-People Partnership; launched on Ugadi, 30 March 2025; rolled out statewide from 19 August 2025.
x: P4 (Public-Private-People Partnership) was launched by CM Naidu and Dy CM Pawan Kalyan at Velagapudi, Amaravati, on Ugadi, Sunday 30 March 2025. It was rolled out statewide only from 19 August 2025, and it was not launched on Republic Day, Independence Day or Diwali.
source: Deccan Chronicle, 31 Mar 2025, 'Naidu, Pawan launch P4 initiative' (deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/andhra-pradesh/naidu-pawan-launch-p4-initiative-1869943, fetched: launched Sunday at Velagapudi); app notes 6:0 (sub 1)
evidence: Deccan Chronicle 31 Mar 2025 (fetched): launch on Sunday at Velagapudi, Amaravati; 30 Mar 2025 = Sunday = Ugadi

x: The Prime Minister's statement was that higher education can be expanded through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) approach, which combines government support with private investment. Outright privatisation, relying on foreign providers, and spending 60% of national income on higher education (an impossible share) were not the approach suggested.
source: general knowledge, not checked (the PM's speech itself was not found locally or on the web; 60% of national income is an impossible figure)
evidence: Local CA library and web search: the original speech was not found; key set from general knowledge (PPP approach in higher education)

from_notes: Biogas is by far the most efficient use of cattle dung. It improves the quality of manure
x: The slurry (digestate) left after biogas is made is a nutrient-rich organic manure, so it is reused as fertilizer for crops. It is not used as cooking fuel (the gas is), animal feed or building material.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 10 p.1; PMF Science & Tech 08 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-08.txt) p.21 (bio-slurry/organic manure replaces chemical fertilisers); Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.155 (GOBARdhan: organic waste into biogas and bio-slurry)

x: Talliki Vandanam pays ₹15,000 per child a year to mothers to cut the cost of schooling, so that fewer children drop out and the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) rises. It does not target GDP directly, it is not limited to admissions in government schools (private and aided schools are covered too), and it is not a literacy-rate scheme.
source: CARE Jul 2026 p.38 (supports continuation of education, reduces dropout risks; Class 1-12 in government, aided, private schools); AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.11 (to reduce financial barriers to education)

from_notes: APCNF stands for Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming
x: APCNF stands for Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming. It was launched in 2016 and is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS), and it won the 2026 Food Planet Prize. 'Centralised', 'Cultivable' and plain 'Community Natural Farming' are wrong expansions.
source: CARE Jun 2026 p.17; Praveen CA-360 May 2026 p.54 (Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming); Praveen CA-360 Jun 2026 p.9

from_notes: EAGLE = Elite Anti-Narcotics Group for Law Enforcement; AP's anti-narcotics task force
x: AP's anti-drug task force is EAGLE (Elite Anti-Narcotics Group for Law Enforcement). It is headquartered at Mangalagiri, has a toll-free number 1972, and the Budget 2026-27 credits it with tackling ganja. ADF, OCTOPUS and SANKALP are not the name of AP's anti-narcotics force.
source: AP Budget 2026-27 speech (src/economy/ap-budget-2026-27-speech.txt) p.13 ('special wing EAGLE' against ganja); CARE Feb 2026 p.28 (AP Eagle toll-free number 1972); app notes 6:1 (sub 7)
